newsitem.title: JAPAN: Too early for Japan to raise interest rates-Angell.
newsitem.headline: Too early for Japan to raise interest rates-Angell.

text.p: Wayne Angell, chief economist at Bear Stearns & Co and a former U.S. Federal Reserve governor, told Reuters in Tokyo on Wednesday that it is premature for Japan to raise its interest rates.
"It's premature to even think about it," he said, speaking after a rise in market interest rates following reported comments from the deputy governor of Japan's central bank.
"Monetary policy cannot be expansionary as long as real estate prices are as weak as they are," he told Reuters. Angell is attending a seminar in Tokyo.

Bank of Japan (BOJ) Deputy Governor Toshihiko Fukui was quoted by an executive of a labour group as saying on Wednesday that the central bank is considering the right timing to raise the official discount rate but it does not want to make a hasty decision.
Japan's official discount rate has been at a historically low 0.5 percent since September 1995.

Angell later clarified his comment on expansionary monetary policy, saying: "The only way to truly judge monetary policy is to answer the question: Does monetary policy cause people to want to sell financial assets and own real assets?"
If it does, monetary policy is expansionary, he said.
He added: "If real estate prices are moving down, then no one wants to borrow money at three percent to buy real estate that's falling 10 percent in value."
